rows.episode_title: Make Your Bark / Pup to the Races
rows.synopsis: Paxton wants to make a mural, but the city council must vote first. The pups try to find common ground with the Goldendoodles.
rows.situation: Paxton spots the big blank wall nobody wants to sit by and pitches a mural, a plan that has to survive a city council vote and, harder, a family of artists who cannot choose between their own paintings. Paw-print votes smear into indecision.
rows.coping: Poppy borrows the city council's own tool, a vote, and when the vote ties into color soup the family reframes the question: not one of our pictures, all of our paws. Every dog in Muttgomery adds a print, and the wall gets its picnic-and-dance-party life back.
rows.notes: mixed age: the paw-print rainbow plays 2-4; an idea going through process, pitch, vote, compromise, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Paxton wants to make a mural, but the city council must vote first' omits the family vote that deadlocks and the paw-print solution. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Paxton wants a mural on the big blank wall, and the idea survives a city council vote only to face a tougher one at home: which family painting wins. Poppy's borrowed voting trick leads to a tie, and the answer is to paint nothing pre-chosen at all, just paw prints for every dog in Muttgomery. The wall becomes the most popular spot in the park.

rows.episode_title: Make Your Bark / Pup to the Races
rows.synopsis: Paxton wants to make a mural, but the city council must vote first. The pups try to find common ground with the Goldendoodles.
rows.situation: The Kibble Cart Derby has a length rule, and the pups all measure too short, so small dogs simply cannot race. Growing takes forever, and the derby happens today.
rows.coping: Pedro flips the constraint: if we cannot be long enough, the carts can be small enough. Trial, error, and doggy-disc wheels later there is a Pup Cart Derby, and the Goldendoodles race them too.
rows.notes: mixed age: the doggy-disc wheels play 2-4; a rule that excludes you being met with redesign rather than surrender, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The pups try to find common ground with the Goldendoodles' belongs to the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The pups are all too short for the Kibble Cart Derby, and Pedro decides the rule is the thing to redesign, not the pups. After stretching fails and big crates smoosh, tiny wooden carts on doggy-disc wheels give birth to the Pup Cart Derby, where racing, not riding, is the point. The Goldendoodles win together, and every dog can race.

rows.synopsis: Puck tries new kibble at a festival. The pups make a movie about city heroes.
rows.situation: Kibble Fest has a hundred flavors and none of them plain, which is the only kind Puck likes, so he plans to go home hungry rather than try. His stomach disagrees audibly, and the family refuses to let the day end.
rows.coping: Nobody forces a bite: the pups kibble-by-committee around him, and Mr. Kibble turns Puck's own safe ingredients into a project. The kibble Puck mixed himself is the one he wants to try, sweet potato and ginger, and he loves it.
rows.notes: mixed age: the mixing-and-baking play 2-4; trying new food on your own terms, with help that offers instead of pushes, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Puck tries new kibble at a festival' omits the no-plain-kibble bind, the stomach commentary, and that the winning bite is self-made. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Puck will not try any of Kibble Fest's hundred flavors, and there is no plain kibble anywhere, so the family plots a no-pressure path: every offer framed as his choice. Mr. Kibble hands him the mixing bowl instead, and the kibble Puck built himself, sweet potato and ginger, is the one he tastes first and loves. Hungry solved, festival saved.

rows.synopsis: Puck tries new kibble at a festival. The pups make a movie about city heroes.
rows.situation: The pups plan Muttgomery's 100th birthday surprise party and forget the two biggest things: a place to have it and anyone to invite. The surprise rule keeps leaking, and the guest list is zero.
rows.coping: Poppy turns the leak into the party: the invitation becomes a parade through town, gathering dogs street by street, celebrating the city out loud at hydrants and lampposts. A forgotten plan becomes the best format for it.
rows.notes: mixed age: the birthday song plays 2-4; a plan that fails and gets recycled into something better, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'the pups make a movie about city heroes' is the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: A surprise 100th birthday party for the city of Muttgomery has treats and a song but no venue and no guests, because planning a surprise is hard. Poppy's fix is to let the surprise parade: invite everyone on the way, celebrate the whole town as they go, and hold the party everywhere. Muttgomery gets the loudest birthday it has ever had.

rows.synopsis: Nana is sad when her exercise class is cancelled. Pretzel's dog park construction project has a few smelly setbacks.
rows.situation: Nana's Paw-laties day, the week's best one, is closed for painting, and every substitute the pups try is too squeezy, too still, or mostly tongue. Nana's tail is down, and Rufus has already gone home.
rows.coping: Pippa's dance party answer needs room, and Sunnyspot has plenty outside: decorations, a dazzle ball, and moves named for the family. Nana's whole class does the waggy wiggle in the yard, and Paw-laties comes back as a party.
rows.notes: mixed age: the Doxie dance moves play 2-4; an older person's disappointment taken seriously and repaired by the kids, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Nana is sad when her exercise class is cancelled' omits the failed substitutes chain and that the replacement becomes Sunnyspot tradition. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Nana's beloved Paw-laties class is canceled for painting, and the pups tour replacement ideas that all flop: gardening too squeezy, tea too still. Pippa's dazzling move-your-body dance party wins, held right in Nana's yard with friends, moves, and a dazzle ball, and the week's biggest disappointment becomes Sunnyspot's first dance party.

rows.synopsis: Nana is sad when her exercise class is cancelled. Pretzel's dog park construction project has a few smelly setbacks.
rows.situation: It is too hot for Puck duck, towers, or twirls, and even hugs are off the menu. Greta cannot leave work to play, and the whole city is panting.
rows.coping: The pups engineer cool: shade from Dad, ice that melts into wading water, a hose-and-watering-can system scaled up from stuff with holes into a Doxie cooldown play zone. Greta gets her turn in the spray, and Puck duck resumes at temperature.
rows.notes: mixed age: the hose-and-can gadgetry plays 2-4; iterating a fix from one pup to a whole city, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'a few smelly setbacks' belongs to the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The heat has canceled every game and even hugs, and Puck's beloved Puck duck is impossible. The pups iterate their way from shade to melting ice to a full backyard cooldown play zone built from hoses and things with holes, then walk the panting city in to cool off. Ms. Pupperpost gets her zip back, and Greta gets sprayed on break.

rows.synopsis: The pups play restaurant with Dill and Delilah. The pups try to help Nana overcome her fear of the dark.
rows.situation: Dill and Delilah are wheat allergic, and the Bowl, the restaurant the whole playdate was built on, has nothing they can eat. Coloring on tables and juke-barks are off the menu with the menu.
rows.coping: The pups rebuild the whole Bowl at home, bench, music, crayons and all, then invent a dish with the allergy in mind, rice, beans, cheese, no wheat. Jules tastes it, puts the No-Wheat Treat on her real menu, and the restaurant becomes somewhere everyone can eat.
rows.notes: mixed age: the restaurant pretend-play 2-4; a friend whose body is different and a place that changes to include them, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'the pups play restaurant with Dill and Delilah' omits the allergy, the home rebuild, and the dish being added to the real menu. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Dill and Delilah's first trip to the Bowl ends before it starts: wheat allergy, nothing safe on the menu, and two kids trying not to spoil the day. The pups rebuild the Bowl at home complete with bench and crayons, invent the No-Wheat Treat, and end up feeding the owner, who adds it to the real menu so everyone can eat there.

rows.synopsis: The pups play restaurant with Dill and Delilah. The pups try to help Nana overcome her fear of the dark.
rows.situation: Delilah's doctor cone keeps her safe and also keeps her from tag, fetch, and hide-and-seek without bonking. She is ready to sit every game out, and Pretzel knows exactly how that feels.
rows.coping: The pups change the game instead of the player: fetch fails, the park opens up room, and Delilah's cone turns out to give super hearing. Poppy's paper cone experiment invents hear-and-seek, a game only Delilah can win, and on the way she finds a lost pup by listening.
rows.notes: mixed age: hear-and-seek plays 2-4; a limitation reframed as a strength, without pretending the loss was not real, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'the pups try to help Nana overcome her fear of the dark' is the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Delilah's medical cone makes every usual game a bonking hazard, and sitting out looks like the only option. The pups redesign play around her, and a paper-cone experiment reveals her super hearing: hear-and-seek is born, and a lost pup gets found by ear on the way. Pretzel, a cone alumnus himself, is the one who keeps looking.

rows.synopsis: The Doxies help a new neighbor feel at home. The pups set up a special party for Nana and her friends.
rows.situation: Gus is new, lost in circles with a list longer than Dad and a face that smiles even when he is worried, and telling him where to go once did not work. He has packages to fetch, kibble to buy, and no bed yet.
rows.coping: The pups try directions, then a tour, then the thing that sticks: a hand-drawn pup map, kibble picture to bed picture to mail. Gus finishes the list without getting lost, learns every P name, and donates the map to City Hall for the next new dog.
rows.notes: mixed age: the map pictures play 2-4; moving somewhere new and not knowing where anything is, and a neighbor who keeps showing up, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The Doxies help a new neighbor feel at home' omits the three-step escalation and the map's second life at City Hall. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Gus Growler arrives with a shopping list longer than Dad and no idea where anything is, and words alone keep him circling. The Doxies escalate from telling to touring to drawing, and the pup map they make, kibble, bed, post office, carries him through the whole list lost-free. The map hangs outside City Hall for the next new dog.

rows.synopsis: The Doxies help a new neighbor feel at home. The pups set up a special party for Nana and her friends.
rows.situation: Dill needs a trim before he can see the red zoomer he is dying to catch, but his waggles are too big for grooming, and story time only half works. Every minute still is a minute not playing.
rows.coping: The pups invent stay-still games, balance pup, Pippa says, statue, and Dill's excitement gets a job instead of a shush. The groom finishes, the zoomer flies, and the waggliest pup in Muttgomery can finally see it.
rows.notes: mixed age: the stay-still games play 2-4; excitement as something to channel rather than cancel, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The pups set up a special party for Nana and her friends' belongs to the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Dill cannot get groomed until he stops waggling, and he cannot stop waggling because the red zoomer is waiting. The pups invent groom games, statue, balance, Pippa says, that give his excitement something to do with itself, and the trim lands in time for fetch. Wholesome, wiggly, solved.

rows.episode_title: The Show Must Bark On! / Dogs at Work
rows.synopsis: The Jazzy Paws' instruments break. The pups create a game for dogs of all sizes.
rows.situation: The Jazzy Paws, three city council dogs, arrive at their own concert with shattered sax, bass, and drums, and the crowd is already on blankets. The show is one broken instrument from cancellation.
rows.coping: Fixing fails and substituting works: Dad as upright bass, bowls as drums, a chew toy as sax, each sound tested against the real thing until the Jazzy Paws have a whole new sound. The concert happens, different and good different.
rows.notes: mixed age: the homemade instrument band plays 2-4; when repair is impossible, replacing with what you have, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The Jazzy Paws' instruments break' omits the failed-repair attempt and the instrument-substitution experiments. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The Jazzy Paws' instruments are wrecked minutes before the concert, and glue-and-tape repairs sound nothing like music. The pups improvise a full set of stand-ins, Dad-bass, bowl-drums, chew-toy sax, and the band premieres a brand-new sound to a full park. The show not only goes on, it gets better.

rows.episode_title: The Show Must Bark On! / Dogs at Work
rows.synopsis: The Jazzy Paws' instruments break. The pups create a game for dogs of all sizes.
rows.situation: The new Bowwow Tower binoculars only work at big-dog height, and the pups see exactly nothing but blue. Jumping, tippy-paws, and Dad all fail, and the best view in Muttgomery is for big dogs only.
rows.coping: Poppy draws the fix, step stools, and asks the construction crew to build them, hard hats included. Every dog uses the binoculars afterward, Nana waves back, and a future construction dog gets hired on the spot.
rows.notes: mixed age: the step stool build plays 2-4; noticing that a public thing excludes some bodies, and getting it changed, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The pups create a game for dogs of all sizes' belongs to the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The Bowwow Tower's binoculars are built for big dogs, and small dogs see only blue sky. After jumping and step-stacking fail, Poppy draws a step stool plan and asks Foredog Frida's crew for help, and the whole family builds them with hard hats on. Every dog in Muttgomery can see the whole city, and Poppy is a future construction dog.

rows.synopsis: Greta takes the day off to join the pups' skate day. The pups make a birthday movie for Gus.
rows.situation: Greta took the day off to watch the pups' rolly tricks, and the city keeps walking into the shot: Ms. Pupperpost, Gus, the whole park. Sidewalk, park, everywhere is crowded, and the day off is melting.
rows.coping: Pedro's chalk line solves the sharing problem in miniature, walking dogs on one side, rolling dogs on the other, and the family turns it into a city-wide proposal. The council votes yes, Foredog Frida paints it green, and Roller-Mama finally gets the whole run.
rows.notes: mixed age: the chalk path plays 2-4; turning a complaint about sharing space into something built for everyone, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Greta takes the day off to join the pups' skate day' omits the crowded-day problem, the chalk prototype, and the council vote. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Roller-Mama's day off keeps getting interrupted by every dog in Muttgomery, until Pedro's chalk rolly path shows the fix: separate lanes for walkers and rollers. A family chalk drawing becomes a council proposal, the construction crew paints it green, and the pups finally run the whole city without stopping once.

rows.synopsis: Greta takes the day off to join the pups' skate day. The pups make a birthday movie for Gus.
rows.situation: The Doxie Baby Boxy opens a box of outgrown baby things, happy tears included, and a real crying baby puppy outside turns the memory into a decision. Grown-up-sized pups cannot use any of it, but Paxton's Wingsy is the hardest goodbye on the blanket.
rows.coping: The pups give almost everything away to babies who need it, then build a Share Box for the park when the blanket overflows, put something in, take something out. Paxton keeps Wingsy until the moment arrives when a napping baby needs him more, and lets go with happy tears.
rows.notes: mixed age: the Share Box ritual plays 2-4; outgrowing beloved things, giving them forward, and happy tears explained honestly, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'the pups make a birthday movie for Gus' is the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The Doxie Baby Boxy full of outgrown baby things meets a crying baby puppy who fits all of it, and the pups start giving their old treasures away. Paxton's beloved Wingsy stays until a baby who cannot nap needs him more, and the blanket overflow becomes Muttgomery's Share Box. Happy tears, explained on screen, become part of the story.

rows.episode_title: Firedogs to the Rescue! / Pup-up Playground
rows.synopsis: The firedogs rescue Greta from a rooftop. The pups help Waffles stand up for herself.

rows.coping: The pups do the thank-you properly, in person and in work: wash the fire truck so the crew can eat dinner and rescue more dogs. Mr. Kibble and neighbors pile on with kibble and woofburgers, and gratitude turns out to be contagious.
rows.notes: mixed age: the truck wash plays 2-4; wanting to thank someone, and finding a way that actually helps them, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The firedogs rescue Greta from a rooftop' omits the pups' unresolved gratitude and the thank-you-in-action structure. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The firedogs save Mayor Greta off a rooftop, and the pups carry an unthanked feeling around until they can act on it: wash the fire truck, free up dinner, free up more rescues. One thank-you pulls the whole neighborhood in behind it, kibble, woofburgers, and all.

rows.episode_title: Firedogs to the Rescue! / Pup-up Playground
rows.synopsis: The firedogs rescue Greta from a rooftop. The pups help Waffles stand up for herself.
rows.situation: Sammy plays Dino Dogs brilliantly all afternoon and then has to go home to a neighborhood with no playground at all. Carrying the volcano to his house is impossible, and the fair-weather fixes, sleepovers, block volcanoes, do not hold.
rows.coping: Puck's pup-up playground is the insight: build small and packable from what the backyard has, pillow mountain, dino toss hoop, bouncy mud lake. Sammy keeps it, packs it at night, and pops it up again every morning.
rows.notes: mixed age: the dino pretend play 2-4; seeing that a friend has less, and giving in a form he can keep, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The pups help Waffles stand up for herself' is the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Sammy is the best Sammysaurus at the playground and the only kid with no playground of his own, and hauling the volcano to his house is a non-starter. The pups build small and packable instead, a pup-up playground of pillow mountains and mud-ball lakes he can store and pop up daily. Generosity that fits in a wagon.

rows.episode_title: Doggie Bags / Fetch Has a New Friend
rows.synopsis: The pups find trash in the park. The pups are ready to celebrate the harvest.
rows.situation: Plastic bags keep blowing out of the recycling and into the perfect leaf piles, and taking them back to Furry Outfitters runs into a real problem: dogs need bags to carry things home. Carrying everything for everyone is not a plan either.
rows.coping: The pups make replacement bags from their own give-away pile, an old sweater with a sewing machine, a T-shirt, a decorated hat-cart system, and offer them at the store. Dogs start making their own, and the plastic stops.
rows.notes: mixed age: the sweater-bag craft plays 2-4; a habit everyone depends on having a replaceable alternative, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The pups find trash in the park' omits the need-for-bags bind and the make-your-own-bag solution. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Wind keeps blowing plastic bags out of the recycling and into the leaf piles, and returning them exposes the catch: shoppers need bags. The pups sew and decorate a rack of alternatives from their Share Box castoffs, and soon the whole store is making its own reusable bags. The leaves stay bag-free.

rows.episode_title: Doggie Bags / Fetch Has a New Friend
rows.synopsis: The pups find trash in the park. The pups are ready to celebrate the harvest.
rows.situation: Delilah's tail-ball smash lands her spinny-ball in the bye-bye spot, where lost things never come down, and every reach, throw, and scrunchie-grabber falls short. Greta's old squeaker is up there too.
rows.coping: The pups escalate to the fire department, and Chief McSpotz's ladder empties the bye-bye spot into a picnic-blanket catch. Then the real invention: bouncy blankets strung below turn the spot into a boing-back net, and tail-ball is forever safe.
rows.notes: mixed age: the blanket boing plays 2-4; a lost thing recovered by asking for bigger help, then a fix that protects everyone, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The pups are ready to celebrate the harvest' is the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Delilah's spinny-ball lands in the bye-bye spot where toys go and never return, and no amount of long-Dog engineering can reach it. Chief McSpotz and her ladder empty a gazillion lost toys into a picnic blanket, and the pups finish the job with a bouncy-blanket trampoline so nothing gets stuck again. Little squeaker comes home.

rows.synopsis: The pups give bows a new life. The pups help Ace through a big change.
rows.situation: Rosie's skin allergy took the fur her beloved bows clip to, and she is at the Share Box to give them all away, Sparkles included. Pippa cannot accept a friend losing her favorite things, but every workaround so far fails: staying still is impossible, and the wig is too itchy.
rows.coping: Dad's tail wig sparks the answer: clip the bow where the allergy never reached. Tail bow, paw bow, collar bow tie, scrunchies from Gigi's give-away box, and Rosie ends up wearing every favorite, with a Sparkles of her own for Pippa.
rows.notes: mixed age: the bow styling plays 2-4; a body change that takes something you love, and redesigning around it, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The pups give bows a new life' omits the allergy, the failed wig, and the tail-clip invention. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Rosie is donating her whole bow collection because a skin allergy took the fur that held them, and Pippa refuses to let that be the ending. Failed fix by failed fix, a very still hold and an itchy wig, Dad's tail wig inspires the answer: bows clip anywhere, tail, paw, collar. Rosie leaves wearing her whole collection, and Pippa wears the twin.

rows.synopsis: The pups give bows a new life. The pups help Ace through a big change.
rows.situation: Puck cannot sleep because tomorrow he finally hides the bone, and counting fetch balls, thank-yous, and lullabies are all losing to the waggly wake-up wizard. Tired tonight means no turn tomorrow.
rows.coping: Pretzel stages a full bedtime adventure, Snuggle Treasure, sleepy potion, fluffy-cloud breathing, and hands Puck the one tool that works: quiet, snuggle, breathe. The wizard vanishes, and Puck owns his own route to sleep.
rows.notes: mixed age: the bedtime adventure plays 2-4 as game; the breathing ritual underneath is a real wind-down tool, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The pups help Ace through a big change' is the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Puck is too excited about tomorrow's bone-hiding turn to sleep, and standard bedtime tricks are failing. Dad's bedtime adventure, Snuggle Treasure, sleepy potion, and fluffy-cloud breathing, smuggles a real relaxation routine in, quiet, snuggle, breathe, and Puck falls asleep empowered to do it again tomorrow.

rows.synopsis: The pups play house with Curly and discover he is scared of loud noises. The pups plant flowers for Nana.
rows.situation: Curly loves playing baby in the house game until garbage day, when the truck's size and claw send him hiding in the house. Songs fail, and the game stalls at its most essential role.
rows.coping: Puck sees the truck through Curly's eyes and then redraws it: a giant Dino-Dog, spots, horns, striped tail, drawn on with the garbage crew's blessing. The scary claw becomes a wagging Diggy twin, and Curly comes out to ride along.
rows.notes: mixed age: the Dino-Dog truck plays 2-4; fear made manageable by renaming the scary thing into a friend, with the adults in on it, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'discover he is scared of loud noises' omits the hiding, the Dino-Dog redesign, and the garbage crew's cooperation. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Curly's house game collapses on garbage day because the truck is a scary giant with a claw, and he hides inside rather than play. Puck and the pups befriend the fear by decorating the truck as a giant Dino-Dog, with spots and horns matching Diggy, and the garbage crew plays along. Curly comes out, pulls the lever, and cheers the tail wag.

rows.synopsis: The pups play house with Curly and discover he is scared of loud noises. The pups plant flowers for Nana.
rows.situation: Paxton draws Nana a butterfly picture and learns Sunnyspot has no butterflies at all, and the pups' first plan, follow them home, fails twice: butterflies follow beauty, not families. Pretzel-as-butterfly does not fool anyone.
rows.coping: The Garden Center supplies the real mechanism: plant the flowers butterflies drink from, zinnias, violets, petunias, honeysuckle. The surprise garden blooms around Nana's door, and the butterflies arrive on their own and stay for everyone at Sunnyspot.
rows.notes: mixed age: the flower planting plays 2-4; you cannot collect a joy, you have to build its habitat, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The pups plant flowers for Nana' omits the failed chasing and the nectar lesson that redirects the plan. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Paxton learns Nana's home has no butterflies, and chasing them home fails because butterflies follow flowers, not fans. A trip to the Garden Center teaches nectar, and the pups plant a surprise garden around Nana's door. The butterflies come by themselves, and everyone at Sunnyspot gets them daily.

rows.episode_title: Pup Fiction / Night at the Pawspital
rows.synopsis: Pretzel reads the pups a bedtime story. The pups help Dragon pick a pet.
rows.situation: Rain traps the pups inside and the library is out of Super Dino-Dog and the Dragon, so the bedtime story they want does not exist. A Betsy Birdy book read as Super Dino-Dog keeps flapping purple wings.
rows.coping: The pups take the story into their own paws: they know every fact about Super Dino-Dog, so they improvise it live, Dad as cave and grumpy dragon, Puppy Corner for zooming room. The invented dragon has a stick in his paw, and the story ends as a real library book.
rows.notes: mixed age: the pretend play 2-4; when the story you want does not exist, authorship is the answer, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Pretzel reads the pups a bedtime story' omits the missing book, the failed Betsy swap, and the kids writing their own ending into the library. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Rain, a missing library book, and a Betsy Birdy substitute that keeps getting corrected by the world's foremost Super Dino-Dog experts lead the pups to write the story themselves. Dad plays cave and grumpy dragon, the dragon's grumpiness turns out to be a stick in the paw, and the improvised adventure ends up shelved in the library as a real book.

rows.episode_title: Pup Fiction / Night at the Pawspital
rows.synopsis: Pretzel reads the pups a bedtime story. The pups help Dragon pick a pet.
rows.situation: Sammy is fine, mostly, but stuck in a hospital bed for one more day with a monitor wired on and friends who get to run. Fetch is impossible, and being a patient is boring.
rows.coping: The pups convert the ward, monitor into space robot, pager into alien transmissions, doctor into alien checkup, and Sammy's bed into a rocket. The play ends with medals, a borrowed paw-pad for drawing Pluto, and a game that can travel.
rows.notes: mixed age: the rocket-bed blastoff plays 2-4; visiting a hospitalized friend and meeting them where they are, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Pretzel reads the pups a bedtime story' is the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Sammy's hurt paw means one more boring day wired to a hospital monitor, and fetch cannot come to him. The pups transform the ward into a space mission, robot, aliens, rocket bed, alien doctor, so the checkup itself becomes part of the game. Sammy keeps the adventure, and the paw-pad, for Pluto.

rows.synopsis: Pedro wants to learn a trick. The pups want to get the most out of their dog park.
rows.situation: Pedro promised Nana a scooter trick he saw once and cannot reproduce, and even with the trick explained the scooter runs away with him. Nana's drumrolls keep ending in a pile.
rows.coping: Rufus names the trick, the hop and twist, and names the blocker, small wheels; Flora the mechanic helps Pedro install bigger ones. The trick gets broken into steps, speed, hop, twist, and Nana gets her drumroll.
rows.notes: mixed age: the trick breakdown plays 2-4; learning something hard by naming it, tooling up, and taking it in steps, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Pedro wants to learn a trick' omits the runaway scooter, the elder-squad help, and the three-step method. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Pedro's promised scooter trick for Nana keeps failing at the whoosh, until a tipoff trail leads to Rufus, who names the trick and its blocker, and Flora, who installs big bouncy wheels. Breaking the hop and twist into three masterable steps turns almost into did-it, and Nana's drumroll finally lands.

rows.synopsis: Pedro wants to learn a trick. The pups want to get the most out of their dog park.
rows.situation: The snow on Mount Muttgomery is real and very far, and the hike eats the pups halfway up: tired paws, tired dad, and a mud patch that stops Pippa cold. Turning back is on the table.
rows.coping: Greta's game breaks the mountain into stripy tree, yellow flowers, giant log, and the family mud-hops the yucky part. The songs carry everyone, including Dad, to the snow, where a snow dino dog and a snowball fight are waiting.
rows.notes: mixed age: the trail games play 2-4; a goal far away eaten one small target at a time, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The pups want to get the most out of their dog park' belongs to the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The Doxies hike for snow on Mount Muttgomery and discover that wanting it and getting there are different things: tired paws, heavy Dad, and one truly yucky mud patch. Greta chops the trail into races to nearby landmarks, the family sings and mud-hops, and the snow arrives with a dino dog and a snowball fight. Even Dad gets carried the last stretch by the same games.

rows.synopsis: The pups search for a lost hamster. The pups help Nana's friends learn new games.
rows.situation: Squeaks the hamster vanishes from his ball mid-snack, and he is the size of a squeak. Sightings multiply while the hamster does not, and the snack trail keeps ending in nothing.
rows.coping: Paxton's poster turns the sightings into a system, and the search ends at the least likely reader: Rufus, whose missing grandpup gave him a tail-downer day, reading the poodle princess aloud to a delighted hamster. Squeaks made everyone's day better on his way home.
rows.notes: mixed age: the poster hunt plays 2-4; a whole community keeping an eye out, and joy found where nobody looked, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The pups search for a lost hamster' omits the sighting-maze, the poster method, and the Rufus ending. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Squeaks escapes into Muttgomery, and every friendly dog has seen him exactly one step ago. Paxton's drawn poster turns the pack into a search network, and the hamster is found at story time, being read The Poodle Princess and the Dogicorn by Rufus, who needed the company as much as the pups needed their pet. Everyone's day goes up a tail.

rows.synopsis: The pups search for a lost hamster. The pups help Nana's friends learn new games.
rows.situation: Pedro wakes up ready for Bark Bark Howl and finds the whole family gone on errands, Dill and Delilah at grandparents, and stuffies that cannot chase. Being an only player in a game built for a circle is a specific kind of lonely.
rows.coping: Pretzel suggests finding other pups, and the search escalates from looking to the Bowwow Tower to a borrowed fire-station megaphone. The howl works, the circle fills with new friends, and the megaphone stays in the park for whoever needs it.
rows.notes: mixed age: the megaphone howl plays 2-4; missing your usual people and finding the move that reaches new ones, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The pups help Nana's friends learn new games' is the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Pedro's ready circle is scattered across Muttgomery on errands, and Bark Bark Howl needs a circle. Pretzel points him outward instead of home: find other pups, from the Bowwow Tower if necessary, and a borrowed fire-station megaphone finally raises the players. The game happens, and the megaphone stays behind for the next lonely pup.

rows.synopsis: The pups build Nana a special drawing. The pups set up a cooking contest.
rows.situation: Paxton needs to draw Nana for the family picture wall before she arrives, and the Doxie house has no quiet anywhere: falling blocks, puppet shows, horsey rides, and finally rain. His drawing smudges, and the deadline is tonight.
rows.coping: The quiet was never a place, it was the pup tent under the table everyone else was already in, and Paxton builds it up with pillows, a dog-bed roof, and borrowed puppet lights. The drawing finishes in his own little castle, and Nana likes it better than a photo.
rows.notes: mixed age: the pillow-tent build plays 2-4; needing quiet in a busy family, and building it rather than demanding it, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The pups build Nana a special drawing' omits the five failed spots and the tent invention. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Paxton has one drawing to finish before Nana arrives and a house full of siblings between him and a single quiet spot. After blocks, puppets, horsey rides, and rain each claim a location, the quiet turns out to have been under the table the whole time, and the family helps him build it into a drawing castle. Nana's portrait hangs on the picture wall, drawn by Paxton.

rows.synopsis: The pups build Nana a special drawing. The pups set up a cooking contest.
rows.situation: The fallen tree blocks the park path and is scheduled for cutting, and it is also the paw-somest climbing, hiding, twirling thing the pups have found all week. What is best for every dog in Muttgomery and what they love are colliding.
rows.coping: Poppy's hunch, save the parts, reshapes the job: branches become a hide-and-seek fort, the trunk gets cut just where it clears the path and becomes an upside-down stage, and the roots move into a jungle gym. The path clears and the tree survives as a playground.
rows.notes: mixed age: the tree fort plays 2-4; a loss bargained down part by part, with safety and the public path respected, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The pups set up a cooking contest' is the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: A wind-felled tree blocks the park path and the sentence is cut it up, but the pups have just discovered its hide-y branches. Negotiation with Foredog Frida salvages everything: a branch fort, an upside-down twirling stage, and a root jungle gym, positioned so the path clears. Nothing is thrown away that can be played on.

rows.synopsis: Russell and Grampy visit the Doxies. The pups want Mama all to themselves.
rows.situation: Russell and Grampy do not bring lunch to the park, and Russell explains it lightly: they do not always have as much food as other dogs. Paxton wants to fix it and discovers his own basket is empty, and Grampy is saving half his sandwich for a friend who is also hungry.
rows.coping: Chef Pax and Chef Dad cook more, Russell teaches his own gravy technique, and Jules proposes the real fix: the Muttgomery Food Fridge, leftover food plus sandwiches, outside The Bowl, with a drawn food sign. No one in Muttgomery has to wait until later.
rows.notes: mixed age: the sandwich assembly plays 2-4; naming that some families work hard and still cannot buy enough food, met with dignity, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Russell and Grampy visit the Doxies' omits the food-insecurity thread, the shared sandwich, and the Food Fridge. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Russell and Grampy have no lunch at the park, and Paxton's sharing instinct meets an empty basket. The response scales: more sandwiches cooked together, then a community Food Fridge at The Bowl stocked by leftovers and kid-drawn signs. Hunger in Muttgomery gets a standing answer.

rows.synopsis: Russell and Grampy visit the Doxies. The pups want Mama all to themselves.
rows.situation: Greta keeps missing the Doxie Dinner Dogs game at work, and the rerun attempt with dirty bowls and bronco obstacles fails honestly. She tells the pups not to rearrange their special thing for her, and she is still a little sad.
rows.coping: The pups take the sadness as a design brief: bedtime already has a story in it, so the Doxie Dream Dogs are born, Fur Brush Knights, Royal Pillow Fluffers, Stuffie Parade, and a Royal Sleep Song with a good night kiss. Mama gets her own special, and the special is bedtime.
rows.notes: mixed age: the bedtime ritual plays 2-4; a parent missing out, a kid noticing, and a new tradition invented so nobody is left out, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The pups want Mama all to themselves' omits the failed rerun, Greta's named sadness, and the Dream Dog invention. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Greta keeps missing the Doxie Dinner Dogs game she never got to play, and the pups' first instinct, rerun it, fails on dirty bowls. Reading her sadness correctly, they invent a second special built where she already is: the Doxie Dream Dogs turn bedtime into Fur Brush Knights, pillow fluffing, a stuffie parade, and a sleep song. Everyone gets their own story with Dad and with Mom.

rows.synopsis: Beau the foster pup comes to town. The pups enter a bike parade.
rows.situation: Beau arrives at Ms. Clawtez's with everything new: home, city, nobody, and the pups know he is scared even though he does not say it. He has never played tail ball, and he does not know a single pup.
rows.coping: The pups teach tail ball one swing at a time, trying what looks hard themselves, then walk Beau to the small park and make the introduction for him. Jasmine and Tazzie suggest a pup meet-up, and Beau ends his first day with a full circle of friends.
rows.notes: mixed age: the tail-ball lessons play 2-4; what a foster move feels like from the inside, and how to introduce a new kid, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Beau the foster pup comes to town' omits the named fear, the failed-first-swing modeling, and the pup meet-up. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Beau the foster pup lands in Muttgomery scared and friendless, and the Doxie pups handle it in two moves: teach him tail ball slowly, failing first so trying again looks normal, then introduce him at the park where the meet-up forms. His first day ends with more friends than some pups make in a year.

rows.synopsis: Beau the foster pup comes to town. The pups enter a bike parade.
rows.situation: All five Doxie pups share one birthday, and each gets a gift they truly want: a skateboard, a jewelry kit, dino stuffies, blocks, a butterfly coloring book. The day of getting immediately meets chances to give.
rows.coping: Pedro lends the brand-new skateboard to a broken mail cart, Paxton colors pages into kite paper, and Pippa sacrifices the necklace string for sparkly kite tassels. Nana names the pattern out loud, and the best birthday is measured in what was given away.
rows.notes: mixed age: the birthday party plays 2-4; new presents being more fun shared than kept, chosen voluntarily, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The pups enter a bike parade' is the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Five Doxie birthdays on one day bring five beloved presents, and by afternoon all the best ones are lent out: the skateboard carries Ms. Pupperpost's mail, the coloring book becomes a butterfly kite, the jewelry string sparkles its tail. Nana says the generous part out loud, and the five-layer cake ends the day.

rows.synopsis: When a heavy snowfall jeopardizes the annual holiday festival, the pups find unique ways to celebrate with all the snowed-in dogs in the city.
rows.situation: Heavy snow buries the annual holiday festival, and the whole city is snowed in with the party cancelled. The celebration the pups were counting on is not happening as planned.
rows.coping: The pups reinvent the festival where the people are: bringing celebration to snowed-in dogs across Muttgomery instead of waiting for the snow to clear.

rows.per_story_synopsis: Snow cancels Muttgomery's holiday festival and strands the whole city, and the pups carry the celebration to the snowed-in dogs instead. The festival happens anyway, one doorstep at a time.
